family: 2 mm pitch GT2 / PowerGrip GT3 timing belt and sprockets
source_url_note: the address printed in the footer of every page of the manual; the PDF itself was hand-collected by the owner (Drive folder, fetched 2026-11-15, vendor_cad/staging/MANIFEST.md) and its download URL was not recorded
title: Gates, Light Power and Precision Drive Design Manual (112 PDF pages)
page_numbering: pages are quoted as PRINTED page numbers; PDF page = printed page + 2
_label: added 2026-11-15. Read since 2026-11-15 by: the ratings verifier (belt.installation_tension.minimum_tst_n, the default installation tension of a Belt, for the motor shaft-load check); gt2_pulley / gt2_idler (belt.stock_widths_mm, for their 'not Gates stock' source text); mechloop/twin/fitted_parameters.json cites belt.converted for the belt stiffness (19 kN per 6 mm)

designation.belt: pitch length (mm), pitch code, width code: e.g. '300 3MGT 09' as printed on p.14; the 2 mm length table lists lengths as 2MR-<pitch length mm> (2MR-74 to 2MR-1700)

stock_widths_mm.note: 12 mm appears in the width multiplier (p.18) and tensioning tables (p.65) but not as a stock width, not in the long-length table and not in the sprocket tables

long_length_table.ref: Table 6 'PowerGrip Long-Length Belting Specifications', p.59 (fiberglass cord). 'Tensile modulus and strength are equivalent to conventional endless and long length belting'

converted.note: 1 lb = 4.44822 N. EA = tension at 0.1 % elongation / 0.001 (a secant value at that elongation)
converted.EA_12mm_note: 12 mm is NOT in Table 6: extrapolated at the 9 mm figure per mm of width

torque_rating.ref: 'Belt Width Selection Tables - 2mm PowerGrip GT3 Belts', p.18: rated torque of the small sprocket, 6 mm belt, before the length factor
torque_rating.teeth_in_mesh: ratings assume 6 or more teeth in mesh on the small sprocket; 5: x0.8, 4: x0.6, 3: x0.4 (p.104)
torque_rating.service_factor: 1.5 to 2.0 recommended for small-pitch drives (p.12); 1.0 on stall / holding torque of a stepper (p.63)

installation_tension.ref: Tables 7 and 8 and Formula 1, p.65. All values are per span
installation_tension.formula: Tst (lb) = 1.21 Q / d + M S^2; Q = driver torque (lb-in), d = driver pitch diameter (in), S = belt speed (ft/min) / 1000
installation_tension.registration_drives: start from the general values times 1.5 to 2.0; 'higher belt installation tensions help in increasing belt tensile modulus'

mass_per_length.ref: not printed. DERIVED from the belt mass constant M (p.65, p.104) and the centrifugal tension formula Tc = M PD^2 rpm^2 / 16.2e6 (p.104), taking Tc = (mass per length) x (belt speed)^2

temperature.note: stock construction; made-to-order constructions on p.71

not_in_the_manual: a tensile modulus or EA figure beyond the one 0.1 % elongation point
a numerical tooth-jump (ratcheting) torque: p.10 only says GT3 resists it better
belt mass per length as a printed figure
12 mm stock belts or sprockets in 2 mm pitch

sprockets.ref: 'Sprocket Specification Tables - 2mm Pitch PowerGrip GT2 Sprockets', p.29 (6 mm) and p.30 (9 mm); diameters also on p.73

minimum_sizes.note: an inside flat idler should be the pitch diameter of a 40-groove sprocket (25.5 mm); 6 teeth in mesh and 60 deg wrap on loaded sprockets

sprockets.bore_note: the 20-groove stock sprocket is listed with a 3/16 in (4.76 mm) plain bore, minimum = maximum; a 5 mm bore is not a Gates stock item

measurement_wang_2018.document: B. Wang, Y. Si, C. Chadha, J. T. Allison, A. E. Patterson, 'Nominal Stiffness of GT-2 Rubber-Fiberglass Timing Belts for Dynamic System Modeling and Design', Robotics 2018, 7(4), 75 (technical note, 8 pages + cover, CC BY)
measurement_wang_2018.page_numbering: printed page numbers of the article; PDF page = printed page + 1

test.specimens: new GT-2 belts, neoprene with glass fibres, free lengths 400 mm and 760 mm, three pulls each (six curves)
test.machine: custom screw-driven manual test stand, 3000 N capacity, 1.6 mm per screw turn, 0.5 turn/s (0.8 mm/s), one reading per turn

break_points_read_from_fig4.ref: Figure 4a / 4b, p.4, read from the plotted crosses (about +/-10 N, +/-0.3 mm, +/-1 MPa)

section_area_mm2_implied.how: force / stress at the six break points (11.9 to 12.0); the paper does not state the area

regression_table1.ref: Table 1, p.5: stress (MPa) = A e^3 + B e^2 + C e + D, e = strain

derived_EA_of_the_tested_belt_n.how: modulus x 12.0 mm2 (equivalently force / strain; independent of what the area really is)

measurement_wang_2018.width_inference: NOT STATED in the paper. The specimens broke at 565 to 670 N. Gates' minimum breaking strength (manual p.59) is 556 N for a 6 mm and 845 N for a 9 mm 2 mm-pitch belt, so the specimens were most likely 6 mm wide. With 9 mm x 1.38 mm the area would be 12.4 mm2, also close to the 12.0 implied, so 9 mm cannot be excluded from the paper alone

if_specimen_was_6mm.basis: low-strain linear fit, scaled with width

measurement_wang_2018.nonlinearity: stiffening from zero load (tangent roughly doubles between 0 and 1 % strain), then softening before rupture at 2.5 to 3.6 % strain. Part of the soft toe may be the grips and belt seating on a manual stand; the paper does not separate it
measurement_wang_2018.hysteresis: not measured: single monotonic pulls to rupture, no unloading, no cycling
